where it consistently achieves the lowest F1 scores up to 255
NLOC. Beyond this threshold, the performance of the LLAMA-
405B model falls below that of the LLAMA-8B, underscoring
the challenges smaller models face in generating user stories,
even for relatively simple code samples.
   In contrast, the performance trajectories of the LLAMA-70B
and LLAMA-405B are similar up to 100 NLOC, at which point
the difference in performance increases. LLAMA-70B model
consistently outperforms the LLAMA-405B across increasingly
complex code samples (> 55 NLOC), and this performance gap
continues to expand as complexity increases. This highlights
that up to a certain number of parameters, higher parameter
count does not necessarily result in a performance increase.               As for the example-based prompting, our findings show that

abling it to match larger models despite parameter limitations. large language models can successfully reverse-engineer user
    As shown in Figure 3, the basic LLAMA-8B configuration stories from source code with at least Adequate-paraphrase
achieves a maximum F1 score of 0.73 across all complexity fidelity. A key finding is that a lightweight 8B model can match
levels when using minimal prompting instructions. One-shot the performance of a much larger 70B model, enabling cost-
and few-shot prompting deliver performance improvements for effective and locally deployable solutions. Looking forward,
LLAMA-8B, allowing it to consistently outperform LLAMA- we plan to extend our approach to larger codebases through

±1% F1 change, and when used without exemplar prompting, gies for code exceeding 200 NLOC. Beyond scalability, we
it improved LLAMA-8B performance beyond the 150 NLOC envision user story recovery as a validation mechanism for
mark. These findings highlight that strategic prompting can AI coding assistants. This verification can detect divergences
improve the performance of smaller models, especially for from user intent, enabling automatic hallucination detection and
medium-complexity code generation tasks. Such tasks, which self-correction. Such validation directly addresses a pressing
reflect typical functionality complexity in practice, provide a need as AI tools become increasingly integrated into software
